sections.overview: The Borbo skipper is a grass-feeding butterfly in the family Hesperiidae, ranging widely through sub-Saharan Africa and nearby islands, with a small European foothold in southern Spain.
sections.identification: Dark brown wings carry translucent forewing spots; a Kenyan guide gives a wingspan of 25–30 mm.
sections.habitat: In southern Spain it occurs along lake margins and waterways, within a small European foothold far from its broad African range.
sections.diet: Larvae eat grasses including sorghum and panic grasses. Polypogon viridis is recorded as a European host.
sections.behavior: Adults fly year-round in Africa but only from May to October in Spain, and avoid the hottest part of the day.
sections.reproduction: The account notes seasonal adult flight, but gives no comparable brood counts across the range.
sections.ecology: Like the related grass skippers Gegenes nostrodamus and G. pumilio, it is tied to open grassy habitats, though Borbo is readily recognized by its translucent forewing spots and has a much broader African range.
sections.conservation: The Taita Hills field guide reports Least Concern, and the species remains widespread, although this regional assessment should not be read as a current global population trend.
